hook_text: Four steps, a seven-metre ramp and a handrail, on one A4 page, so exact a builder needs no ruler.
clip_script: The brief gives numbers: rise 600, four risers of 150, treads 250, width 1 200, ramp 7 200 at 1 in 12. Scale 1:50: divide everything by 50 in a little table, once. Front view: stairs as a rectangle with lines at 3, 6, 9, ramp as a plain face, rails 18 up. Drop feint lines and draw the plan underneath: four treads of 5, a ramp 144 long, a landing of 24. Project across for the side view on the right: the sawtooth of four steps, and the ramp behind them dashed, because it is hidden. Fix the lines, dark, feint, dashed. Write the real sizes once each: 4 at 150, 7 200, 900. Title block, 1:50, first angle symbol. Done. A builder could set it out tomorrow.
visual_style: Whiteboard A4 outline; a front view appears, feint lines drop to a plan, lines sweep right to a sawtooth side view with a dashed ramp; dimensions pop on one by one.
mood: Methodical, building to a satisfying finished sheet.
pacing: Table, front, plan, side, lines, dimensions, title block: seven beats.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw the plan of your own front steps at 1:20.
